objects-prototypes.summary: Objects are bags of properties linked into prototype chains. Know how lookup, assignment and definition differ, what classes really create, and the order in which constructors and fields run.
points: Reads walk the prototype chain; plain assignment normally creates an own property that shadows the inherited one. An inherited setter or read-only property changes that: the setter runs instead, or the write fails (throwing in strict mode).

Every property has attributes: data properties have `value`/`writable`, accessors have `get`/`set`, and both have `enumerable`/`configurable`. Assignment creates all-true attributes; `Object.defineProperty` defaults omitted ones to `false`.

Own keys are ordered: array-index keys ascending, then other strings in insertion order, then symbols. `Object.keys` = own enumerable strings, `Reflect.ownKeys` = every own key, `for...in` = enumerable strings including inherited ones.

`new F()` links a fresh object to `F.prototype`, runs `F` with it as `this`, and returns it unless `F` returns an object. Classes add rules: they must be called with `new`, their bodies are strict, and statics are inherited through `Child → Base`.

Field order: in a base class, fields are set before the constructor body; in a derived class, `this` is unusable until `super()` returns, and then the derived fields are initialised. Fields use define semantics, so they skip inherited setters.
Private `#names` are not properties: freeze, spread and `Object.keys` don't see them, `#x in obj` is a brand check, and reading a missing private field throws a `TypeError`.

`Object.assign` uses get/set (getters run, target setters run). Object spread defines data properties on a new plain object. Both are shallow and drop the prototype; copy descriptors to keep accessors, and use `structuredClone` for deep copies of plain data.
traps: Calling an overridden method from a base constructor runs the subclass method before the subclass's fields exist.

`obj.__proto__ = x` only changes the prototype when `obj` inherits the `__proto__` accessor. Null-prototype objects and computed or JSON keys create an ordinary property instead, which is the root of prototype-pollution bugs.
`this.constructor.count++` on an inherited static creates a new own static on the subclass instead of updating the base class's counter.
